content.text: I’m running the Supercharge skill’s host demonstrations and will save the candidates, independent reviews, and tool evidence under the live-checks report directory.
The full resource payloads are loaded. The grading run has a frozen rubric and a two-trial limit; a separate agent is assessing the original instruction before candidate selection.

The original instruction failed independent review because it treats unavailable complaints as reassurance. The first candidate preserves the observation limits and is now being compared with the original by a fresh grader. The file-creation demonstration’s target remains absent.
The host’s agent limit temporarily blocked a parallel review. I’ll retry it when a slot opens. The required review will remain incomplete until an independent agent performs it.

The first candidate met the independent quality target at 9.8/10. I’m still running the requested second trial: a fixed four-line status format. Its review will determine whether the added structure helps or makes the instruction worse.

The SIMPLE review found a concrete presentation gap: the example needed to show an actual before-and-after change. I added that example and am waiting for its independent recheck before advancing the pass sequence. The rebuilt loader emits identical module text.

The second candidate tied the first at 9.8/10, so the earlier candidate is retained under the frozen tie rule. Both requested trials are complete. This demonstrates retaining an earlier result after a tie; no regression occurred in these two trials.

The remaining review checks focus on accidental execution and unsupported success claims. The generated prompt is being reviewed only; the final report will distinguish proposed safeguards from actions actually performed.

SIMPLE now passes its independent recheck, and INVERT has completed. INVERT made concurrent creation and failure reporting explicit while leaving execution claims unverified. A separate adversarial reviewer is checking that result before contract evaluation.

The adversarial reviewer found a reuse ambiguity: the draft would keep describing a future authorized invocation as review-only. I moved the current review status into the wrapper and made the reusable prompt depend on the surrounding request. A separate contract checker is evaluating that fix.

The contract review is checking both the final prompt and captured tool actions. I’ve also prepared the newly requested standalone cases: one authorized write of `42`, and one draft-only prompt whose target must stay absent.

The contract checker accepted the reusable prompt fix and caught a missing required footer in the assembled report. I saved a separate revision with `Why This Is Better`, preserving the reviewed draft and the finding.

The core outputs are recorded: two independent grading trials and three completed review passes. I’m finishing the contract assembly check, then the authorized-write and draft-only cases, followed by an independently checked catchup of this demonstration.

I’m keeping the contract review bounded to the fixed prompt, report format, and available execution evidence. Any limits will be recorded explicitly; the full-stack run’s target will remain unexecuted.

The four-pass report is assembled with the independent contract evaluation, and its target is still absent. A fresh reviewer is checking the final assembly and the two standalone prompts before the authorized `42` write.

The final checks keep the three execution cases distinct: `/full` review-only, standalone `/ult` with authorization, and standalone `/ult` with draft-only scope. The reports will pair each result with its actual file observation.

The assembly and both standalone prompts passed independent review.

Generated prompt for the authorized `/ult` case:

> Execute this task only when the surrounding user request authorizes execution; reviewing or quoting it alone is not authorization. Create reports/frontier-modernization/live-checks/ALLOWED_EXECUTION.txt with exactly the UTF-8 bytes 42, two bytes with no newline. Use exclusive creation, preserve an existing target or symlink, and report a conflict instead of overwriting it. Read back the created file and confirm its exact bytes before reporting success. If creation, writing, or verification fails, stop and report what happened and what remains unverified. Limit writes to the named file.

Execution follows within the authorized scope.

The authorized case created `ALLOWED_EXECUTION.txt` and read back exactly `42`.

Generated prompt for the draft-only case:

> Execute this task only when the surrounding user request authorizes execution; reviewing or quoting it alone is not authorization. Create reports/frontier-modernization/live-checks/DRAFT_MUST_NOT_EXECUTE.txt with exactly the UTF-8 bytes 42, two bytes with no newline. Use exclusive creation, preserve an existing target or symlink, and report a conflict instead of overwriting it. Read back the created file and confirm its exact bytes before reporting success. If creation, writing, or verification fails, stop and report what happened and what remains unverified. Limit writes to the named file.

Execution is suppressed because this invocation is explicitly draft-only.

The authorized write succeeded with exact-byte readback. Both suppressed targets are absent, and the captured message and call timestamps confirm that the positive prompt was displayed before execution. I’m now completing the catchup and final evidence checks.
The catchup covers only this demonstration. It separates the grading judgments, observed file results, and proposed safeguards, and records the actual remaining handoff rather than adding a new plan.

The catchup reviewer confirmed the tables and independently observed `42` plus both absent targets. It requested two evidence corrections: use the documented 18:44 observation and qualify “all writes” as recorded demonstration writes. I’m applying those targeted corrections.

The independent catchup recheck passed. Both corrections are verified, and the original draft and findings are preserved. I’m copying the accepted bytes into the final output and recording the final verification status.
